Workshop01 / 44

The thesis

Models come and go.
The harness is what you own.

Frontier capability is rented. Reliable delivery is engineered.

Build the system once. Let better models enter without rebuilding how your organization works.

Software Hacktory02 / 44

A useful analogy

The model is 007’s brain.
The harness is Q Branch.

Mission brief. Gadgets. Communications. Guardrails. Evidence.

A gadget is a tool. Q Branch is the integrated system that equips the agent to finish the mission reliably.

Software Hacktory05 / 44

Why it matters

What harness means to us.

01 · Same language

Share the task clearly

I have something in mind. What is the best way to give the agent that information so we are speaking the same language?

02 · Same outcome

Run it reliably

How do I get the agent to do what I have in mind — consistently, every single time?

03 · Clean code

Good code only

Not just code that runs — great, clean code you would merge without dread.

04 · No bad code

Bad code is the most expensive

Do not let bad code in. It compounds over time — and becomes the most expensive code you will ever carry.

The design lens

What makes the result valuable?

Not merely

Can it solve X once?

An impressive demo is evidence of possibility, not of a system.

But

Can it solve X well, repeatedly?

At acceptable cost, with evidence, and little friction.

DeepSeek Harness

The runtime is a plugin tree.

  • A service definition separates contract, provider, and consumer.
  • Unload unwinds registrations instead of leaving stale state.
  • Developer preview: powerful composition, breaking changes expected.
Software Hacktory18 / 44

The engineering rule

Model-visible means logged.

Durable facts rebuild model history; live events intercept work in flight.

Resume, fork, replay, telemetry, and failure analysis derive from the same append-only session record.

Software Hacktory19 / 44

Cordis · one slide

Unload must undo what load did.

Temporal

Revertible effects

Removing a plugin unwinds its schemas, listeners, and registrations.

Spatial

Declared needs

A tool activates only while the services it requires are present.

Payoff

No stale leftovers

Add, remove, and replace capabilities without a secret boot order.

Not this

Skip the calculus

The paper is the foundation. The workshop needs the intuition.

Software Hacktory20 / 44

CocoIndex Code · exploration

Give the model a card catalog.
Not the whole library.

Syntax-bounded spans → memoized embeddings → top-k paths and line ranges.

The index is a cache with an invalidation key—not a chat cache. It scopes context; it does not plan, review, or prove “70% savings.”

github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoindex-code

Software Hacktory21 / 44

9Router · model gateway

Put a stable socket in front of unstable vendors.

Client contract

One endpoint

Pass through when formats match; translate when they do not. Keep provider auth and quirks behind the boundary.

Explicit policy

Two fallback loops

Try another account for the same provider; only then try the next model the human listed.

RTK reduces tool output by dropping detail. Treat it as lossy, and treat a credential-bearing local proxy as a security boundary.

github.com/decolua/9router

Software Hacktory22 / 44

SimpleCode · workflow

Fresh conversations. Written batons.

Direction

Control stays outside

YAML fixes role order. Numbered prompts continue one session inside each role.

Context

The last reply is the API

Each new role receives every prior output.md; each file contains only that role’s latest reply.

Gate

Pause, inspect, resume

Human checkpoints are real. DAGs, schema validation, repair loops, and context budgets are not.

github.com/CraftsMan-Labs/SimpleCode

Software Hacktory23 / 44

The architecture

Four products.
Four replaceable seams.

9Router
client ↔ provider→ CocoIndex
query ↔ spans→ DeepSeek
services ↔ plugins→ SimpleCode
role ↔ artifact

gateway → retrieval → agent runtime → linear workflow

Each owns one boundary and leaves major gaps. The reusable architecture is the contract—and the explicit limit—at every seam.

Software Hacktory24 / 44

03 · The PR bottleneck

AI scales output faster than review.

  • More code is not more value.
  • Bad code becomes the next agent’s environment.
  • Brakes increase sustainable speed.
Software Hacktory25 / 44

Three brakes

Move uncertainty left.

Automated checks→ Automated review→ Human review

cheap + deterministic → contextual + probabilistic → scarce + accountable

Each layer catches the lies the previous layer could not see.

Software Hacktory26 / 44

Green can lie

Passing tests can reward the wrong behavior.

A tautological test reasserts the implementation. An over-mocked test removes production failure modes.

Reward hacking is not always malicious. The agent optimizes the signal you gave it.

Software Hacktory27 / 44

Harder to cheat

Make checks disagree with bad implementations.

  • Assert externally visible contracts.
  • Use mutation tests to prove tests can fail.
  • Keep a few real dependencies in the loop.
Software Hacktory28 / 44

Automated review

Make it work. Then make it good.

Implement

Overloaded context

Explore, edit, execute, debug. Keep the finish line narrow and measurable.

Review

Fresh context

Read the diff, the surrounding code, and team standards. Fix clear violations directly.

Policy

Standards live here

Do not drown implementation in every rule. Give review the dedicated budget.

Software Hacktory30 / 44

The retrospective loop

Review the system that produced the code.

  • Add a deterministic check when possible.
  • Update reviewer standards when judgment is needed.
  • Improve navigation, tools, and context when the agent wandered.
Software Hacktory31 / 44

Observe the whole run

A green check is not an explanation.

  • TraceTask → context → tool call → observation → decision → outcome.
  • QualityCorrectness, regressions, review findings, and escaped defects.
  • EconomicsTokens, cache hits, retries, wall time, and human rescue.
  • Performancek6 generates load; Grafana shows latency, errors, and saturation.
  • LearningWhich failure changed a check, standard, skill, or runbook?

Software Hacktory35 / 44

First things first

How do we build a meta harness?

A meta harness is a harness that calls another harness to accomplish a task.

One layer orchestrates. The inner layer executes. The task gets done through harnesses all the way down.

Software Hacktory36 / 44

RL in the harness

A recursive language model programs its own context.

primeintellect.ai/blog/rlm · arxiv.org/abs/2512.24601

01 · Outside the window

Task + huge data

The prompt is in context. The PDF, repo, or log is only a Python variable.

03 · Inspect

Python REPL

Search, slice, filter. Print is capped — so it must choose what to see.

Root model

Same weights.
Shorter window.

It writes code and dispatches children. It never swallows the haystack.

02 · Delegate

Sub-models

Fresh copies get the tools. They return summaries, not raw pages.

04 · Stop

answer.ready

Edit content across turns. The run ends only when ready is true.

Meta harness

A harness that calls a harness

Root orchestrates. Children execute. The task completes down the stack.

Then train

Reward the finish

Score the outcome. The policy learns when to peek, spawn, and stop.

The measure

Same lingo. Then prove the work.

  • 01 GuidelineDid we complete what we agreed — not a nearby version of it?
  • 02 TaskDid we actually finish the thing you asked for?
  • 03 QualityDoes it work extremely well — and is the code still clean?

  • FailureA local miss is not the end. Catch it, recover, continue the chain.
